sense: familiar with, acquainted with (a subject or a place)

terms.grammar: adjective, with the genitive (or the ablative)
evidence: Cic. Off. 1.147: doctōs hominēs vel ūsū perītōs (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Familiar with something from having done it; the opposite is imperītus.

evidence: Plaut. Rud. 1.3.28: nec locī gnāra sum (Lewis & Short)
terms.comment: Rare but classical (Lewis & Short); its opposite, ignārus, is the commoner word.

terms.gloss: well versed in, at home in
terms.grammar: participle of versor, with in + ablative
evidence: Cic. Quinct. 3: in hāc multum et saepe versātus (Lewis & Short, s.v. versō)
Cic. Rep. 3.4: virī in rērum pūblicārum varietāte versātī
terms.comment: Familiar with a field from long dealing with it.

phrases.english: and I don’t know my way around here

phrases.latin: Ego hujus regiōnis imperītus sum; tū viam mōnstrā.
phrases.english: I don’t know this area; you show the way.

sources: Lewis & Short: peritus · Lewis & Short: gnarus · Lewis & Short: verso
